classification.difficultyReason: Identify similar right triangles formed by heights and shadows, then use corresponding-side ratios to calculate the tower height.

content.prompt: A tower standing on level ground casts a shadow 40 m long. A vertical stick 3 m high is placed at the tip of the shadow. The stick is found to cast a shadow 6 m long. Find the height of the tower.

answer.worked:
The tower and stick form right triangles with their respective shadows. Both triangles have the same angle of elevation of the Sun, so they are similar by AAA.

Let the tower height be $h$ metres. Matching heights and shadow lengths gives
$$\begin{align*}\frac{h}{3}&=\frac{40}{6}\\h&=\frac{3\times40}{6}\\h&=20.\end{align*}$$
The tower is $20\text{ m}$ high.
